label: Plan
payload:
1) Clarify scope and acceptance criteria for the requested software change, including affected components, user-visible behavior, and deployment constraints.
2) Inspect the current codebase and interfaces to identify impacted modules, dependencies, configuration, and any migration requirements.
3) Design the minimal-change implementation approach, defining code changes, data/model changes if any, API/UI contract impacts, feature flags/rollback strategy, and backward-compatibility considerations.
4) Implement the change in small, reviewable increments with unit/integration coverage for modified behavior and error paths.
5) Run local/static validation (build, lint, unit/integration tests) and fix defects before handoff to end-to-end testing.
6) Execute browser/end-to-end tests against the changed flow and verify acceptance criteria, regressions, and observability signals.
7) If tests fail, analyze failures, update the plan to address root causes, implement fixes, and rerun validation/testing before requesting deployment.
8) After reviewer approval and green tests, prepare deployment notes including rollout steps, monitoring checks, and rollback instructions for DevOps.
Risks: unclear requirements, hidden dependency/regression risk, breaking API/UI/data contract changes, migration/config issues, insufficient test coverage.
Validation approach: reviewer approval of plan, automated build/lint/unit/integration checks, browser end-to-end tests for primary and regression flows, post-deploy smoke/monitoring checks.
